per_shot.note: Real ceiling with panels, beams and fixtures, ribbed riveted walls and dusk portholes; the polished floor carries warm streaks from every light, so the stock room already feels warm, but the walls are one beige.
Warm and lived-in for a stock room; the reflections spill the porthole dusk onto the floor; the teal monitor smear on the floor reads a little like an artifact.
Fridge, corkboard and crates sit in a warm pool; the dark wing doorway on the right gives some contrast; the bays still repeat the same cone of light.
The fern, the patterned rug, the radio with its glowing dial and the books all read; the room is clearly richer than stock and the floor glow ties it together.
The star chart, arc lamp and book shelf read well; the arc lamp warms the floor, though its cone on the wall is weaker than in B.
The best frame: kettle and cups, a bunk with pillow and blanket, a lit Gallery doorway, the arc lamp over the star chart. Warm and cared-for, with strong floor reflections.

top_issues.issue: Walls are one flat beige in every bay, and the same downlight cone repeats identically along them
top_issues.why: It reads as an institutional corridor more than a home; the brief asks for value variation across surfaces and dark corners for contrast.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Vary the panel values (darker lower band or insulated quilted panels in some bays, a lighter accent panel), let some bays fall darker between pools, and put the warmth around the furnished slots rather than evenly along the wall.

top_issues.issue: The floor reflections are strong vertical streaks, and a teal smear sits in empty floor
top_issues.why: The warm spill on the floor is right, but the long streaks read as wet lacquer or a screen-space artifact more than lit floor plating, and the teal smear pulls the eye away from the suit.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the warm floor pools but lower the gloss so the reflections become soft blurred pools; damp the reflection of the monitor's emissive.

top_issues.issue: The practicals don't visibly land on the wall: the arc lamp, radio and bunk sconce barely tint the masonry around them
top_issues.why: The direction says the arc lamp and practicals pool warm light on the wall; here the ceiling cones do the lighting and the bought lamps read as props.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the arc lamp a clear warm pool on the wall and floor beneath its shade, add a small glow around the radio dial, and make the bunk sconce wash the bedding.

top_issues.issue: Small furnishings are close to the threshold of readability at play scale
top_issues.why: The rug sits flat and narrow and the cups and books are tiny, so in the gameplay frame they read as a stripe and specks.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise the contrast of the rug pattern and lift its edge, and let the light over the galley and the shelf pick out the kettle and the book spines.

Dusk portholes as the warm signature
The suit, lit by its own pool, as the most legible thing in the frame

Warm light spilling onto the floor
The lit Gallery doorway with its placard

per_shot.note: Same shell and ceiling as A, but the matte floor keeps the warmth only at the wall line; the lower third of the frame is a near-black slab.
Honest matte plating with clear seams, but the porthole dusk does not reach the floor and the foreground is dead dark, which reads grim more than sanctuary.
A small warm pool at the fridge base is nice; a floor seam runs straight through the suit; the large dark foreground again.
The furnishings read as well as in A; the room is clearly richer than stock, but the floor in front of them is cold and empty.
Better than A here: the arc lamp throws a visible warm cone onto the wall and fridge, so its light lands. The foreground is still black.
Same rich dressing as A; the arc lamp cone lands on the star chart; the dark foreground and a seam line through the suit cost it.

top_issues.issue: The bottom 35-40% of the frame is an unlit, near-black floor slab
top_issues.why: The brief wants a warm sanctuary with dark corners for contrast; this is a dead foreground that adds no information and makes the home feel cold.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Bring the camera's floor edge up or end it with a lit trim, and carry warm pools and porthole spill further forward on the floor.

top_issues.issue: The porthole dusk does not spill onto the floor
top_issues.why: The direction explicitly calls for dusk from the portholes on the floor; here it stops at the glass.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a soft warm patch on the floor under each porthole, or a little gloss so the dusk reads on the plating.

top_issues.issue: Walls are one flat beige in every bay, and the same downlight cone repeats identically along them
top_issues.why: It reads as a corridor more than a home; there is little value variation between surfaces.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Vary the panel values and materials bay to bay, leave darker gaps between pools, and concentrate the warmth around the furnished slots.

top_issues.issue: A floor seam line runs vertically through the suit in the east frames
top_issues.why: It cuts across the most important figure in the frame and slightly hurts its legibility.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Offset the plating seams from the suit's resting line, or lower the contrast of the seams where the suit's pool lands.

top_issues.issue: The radio, bunk sconce and galley light barely wash their surroundings
top_issues.why: Light should land; the small practicals read as props.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each practical a small warm wash on the wall and the object beside it.
